entries.text: At 5:22 a.m., only the mixing desk and wall clock lit the control room. Outside, black sky was turning deep blue.
I'm not late, am I? The stairwell lights have already gone out on three floors.
We have eighteen minutes. Listen once first. I just cleared the last patch of noise.
The transmitter lamp glowed quietly. Today it would go dark only once more.
So this really is our last shift. Saying it aloud makes it sound less real.
Shutdown is at 5:40. Before then, the archive gives us one sixty-second receiving window.
You said we should leave a station call in that window. We still haven't chosen one?
We can send only once. The archive won't open a second connection; this is the old station's final record number.
Zhou set a reel with a faded label beside the deck. Its date was thirteen years old.
I found it at the back of storage. That was my first morning shift alone.
No wonder I didn't recognize you. Your voice was much brighter then.
And much faster. I thought one slow second would keep the whole mountain from hearing us.
The reel began to turn. After a brief hiss, a younger voice woke in the monitor speaker.
“This is Cape Hill Community Radio. Good morning. May someone hear you today.”
The words are old, but they don't sound far away. You cleaned it up almost too well.
I only joined the breaks. I left the breaths in. Those should stay.
After the final word, the level needle eased back to zero.
If the archive takes this, it remembers what the station used to be.
Right. Or we record something now, so it remembers how we sounded before shutdown.
Can't we join them? Sixty seconds is enough.
One transmission becomes one archive record. A splice marks both parts as edited, not as our final live call.
Then we aren't choosing which sounds better. We're choosing what we want it to prove.
The clock reached 5:27. On the roof, wind tapped a cable against the antenna.
The old call proves how long this place endured. A new one proves we were here when it ended.
Both are true. Let's not make someone in the future guess. We can choose for ourselves.
Lin moved the send switch to standby. The deck and microphone lamps lit together, waiting for one to be chosen.
The archive window permits one final transmission.
Send the restored station call
Record a new call for this moment
